name: Densest k-Subgraph
problem_statement: Given an undirected graph and integer k, find exactly k vertices maximizing the total value of edges induced by those vertices.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Collapse parallel edges by summing nonnegative weights; use unit weight in unweighted mode.

problem_inputs.name: k
problem_inputs.description: Exact number of vertices to select.

problem_inputs.name: weight_mode
problem_inputs.description: Use unit edge values or nonnegative input weights.

problem_inputs.name: solution_quality
problem_inputs.description: Whether a nonoptimal solution is permitted.

required_outputs.name: induced_edge_value
required_outputs.description: Number or weight sum of edges induced by the result.

optional_outputs.name: upper_bound
optional_outputs.description: Certified upper bound on the optimal induced edge value.

solution_semantics.objective: Maximize induced edge count or nonnegative weight over vertex sets of cardinality exactly k.
solution_semantics.exactness: Exact mode requires optimal=true; approximate mode returns a feasible set and any known bound.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Return one best solution unless tied solutions are explicitly requested in a future extension.

validation_rules: The result contains exactly k unique input vertices.
Recomputed induced edge value equals the reported value.
optimal=true is valid only when no feasible k-set has a larger objective.
edge_cases: k=1 always has induced edge value zero in a loop-free graph.
k equal to the vertex count selects the whole graph.
No feasible solution exists when k exceeds the vertex count.
